analysis:
This pass examined the Autopilot protocol and state changes.

- CoordinatorClientState.swift (head 245-263): the separate autopilotInventory accessor is replaced by publishModelAutopilot and modelAutopilotRegistration, which write and read the snapshot and inventory together under one unfair lock. registeredAutopilotInventoryIDs was also added. This is an atomicity improvement and has no security regression.

- ModelAutopilot.swift (head 31-49, 80-161, 198-244): adds optional additive telemetry fields to the snapshot: capabilities, adopted/held models, busy reasons, transition stalls and download storage. It also adds ModelAutopilotCommand.holdSeconds (doc says 0...86_400) and ModelAutopilotStatus.detail. These fields are provider-to-coordinator advertisement data. They are self-reported by an adversarial provider (ADV-001), so the coordinator must treat them as untrusted, consistent with T-007/T-012/T-027.

- New attack surface: download_storage reports disk free/reserve/used bytes and operator caps. This is additional host fingerprint telemetry, which is low sensitivity and not prompt-derived. No A-001 data or T-041 cache identity (HMAC tags) appears in these fields.

- Decoding (head 33-69): strict required/optional decoding, unchanged behavior.

- ModelAutopilotBusyReason.swift: closed enums only.

- ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift (unit 0 metadata only; the patch is visible only in file_changes):
  - Adds superviseTransitions, sweepAutopilotCachedBuilds, refreshAutopilotDownloadStorage and refreshAutopilotInventoryRegistration to the tick.
  - Subtracts autopilotHeldWeightBytes from reclaimable MLX, using min() to guard against underflow.
  - The implementations are not supplied.

Open questions for integration:
1. The holdSeconds bound (0...86_400) is not enforced in the visible decoder. The clamping site is not visible; a coordinator-sent huge value could pin memory. The coordinator is trusted, so the impact is availability only.
2. The inventory_downloads capability implies prefetch_model can trigger model downloads into the Autopilot set. Download source, revision and hash verification (T-012/T-027 weightHash, A-004) and disk-reserve enforcement (T-016) are not in the supplied evidence and need review.
3. Adopted models keep serving without a lease. Integration should confirm that adoption still requires verified weight hashes and the existing serving authorization (TB-011/A-016).
